title: The Angular CLI: generating, building, testing and updating a version

videos.script:
Today the planner gets a folder, and you meet the one command you will type more than any other. {{new}} ng new writes a whole project at once. On the day this course was recorded, its last step failed. npm stopped with an error about something called edgesOut, inside npm itself. {{fix}} You will see why, and the one line that gets past it. Then every version in the project is written down exactly, so your project and this one install the same code.

Then four commands, each with a job. {{serve}} ng serve builds the app and keeps rebuilding it while you work. You change the heading, and the open page changes without a reload. {{look}} You also save a small program called look, which reads a page from the terminal, so the transcripts can show you what the browser shows.

{{generate}} ng generate writes a component in four files that agree with each other. {{build}} ng build writes the files a real server sends, and you serve them the way a host would. One address breaks there, on purpose, and it explains a setting every Angular host needs. {{test}} ng test runs the tests. One fails, because you changed the heading, and you fix it.

Last, ng update. {{update}} It offers Angular 22, and refuses twice when you ask for it. Once because you have not committed, and once because of the Node version. Both refusals are useful, and both are worth reading slowly.
